brief: Rates are stabilizing: Treasury auctions were well absorbed and bond volatility has retraced about 30% of its recent move, a first calm stretch in rates. In Asia, Korean memory names sold off (Kospi -3 to -4%, Samsung/Hynix -4%) after CXMT unveiled a new 4F² DRAM architecture and China's roughly 10% DRAM share keeps growing, adding to concern about peak memory earnings despite strong fundamentals; Samsung's results missed expectations. US hedge fund positioning reversed September's trend: Info Tech was the most net-sold sector this week (-1.0 SDs) after being most-bought in 4 of the prior 5 weeks, funds rotated into Industrials instead, and fundamental long/short net exposure sits at 52.9%, the 6th percentile over the past year. On AI, Google is reportedly testing a model, Carbon, competitive with Opus 5.5, and Polymarket prices Google as a serious best-model contender. GS's core argument: compute scarcity, not model leadership, is the durable edge, since the market doubts the street can bring power and data center capacity online quickly, so leadership rotates quarterly while hyperscalers' ownership of scarce compute lasts longer. September CPI, Wednesday, consensus 0.6% headline/0.2% core, is the week's main event; a 10bp downside surprise on core would matter for rates.
